These are words you use to talk about injuries and accidents.
Example: He was seething afterwards because he couldn't go to the competition.
to stop without finishing an activity (e.g. school, a contest)
Example: He had to drop out of the competition.
to inhale and exhale from the body
Example: The ball went thundering down the lane.
There are two ways of pronouncing the /th/ consonant blend sound in English.

1. Unvoiced.
You do not use your vocal chords to make the sound. You do not feel any vibration.
Touch the front of your neck as you say the words. Can you feel any vibration when you say the /th/ sound? You shouldn't.

1. Voiced.
It is made by putting the tongue between or just behind the teeth. The tongue presses and then moves away.
Touch the front of your neck as you say the words. Can you feel any vibration when you say the /th/ sound? You should.
Can you try this tongue twister?
Thirty-three thirsty, thundering fathers thumped Mr. Thurber on Thursday.
Intonation is important in long questions. You use the rise and fall of your voice to show the listener when you are or are not finished.
In long questions, the intonation falls and then rises to show the question is not finished. The intonation rises or falls at the end, depending on whether it is an information or yes/no question.
Say these sentences. Vary the intonation on the bolded words. Be sure to notice if the question is an information or yes/no question.

Should I be wearing thicker socks since these bowling shoes are thoroughly disgusting?

The ball went thundering down the lane and into the gutter and I didn't even get a strike?

How many times a week do you have to practice if you want to be a better bowler?

images.text:
Vanessa: Sal, let's think about lessons later. Let's bowl!
Sally: You're right. I don't know if I'm wearing the right clothing for this. Should I be wearing thicker socks since these bowling shoes are thoroughly disgusting?
Vanessa: My socks are thin, too!

Sally: My brother used to bowl all the time.
Vanessa: Why did he stop?
Sally: He hurt his thumb. He twisted it in one of the holes in the bowling ball.
Vanessa: Ugh - sounds terrible!
Sally: Yeah, he was seething afterwards because he had to drop out of the competition.
Vanessa: That's too bad! OK, I'm going to try and bowl my first one. Ready?
Sally: OK, remember to breathe ...

Vanessa: Ouch!
Sally: What happened!
Vanessa: I twisted my thumb! My thumb is throbbing! The ball fell on my foot, too. Oww! The ball went thundering down the lane and into the gutter and I didn't even get a strike? Wow, maybe I should reconsider those lessons.
Sally: No kidding! There's a class on Thursday. Should I sign us up?
Vanessa: I can't move right now, Sal!
